https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-conse.text: European People’s Party leader Manfred Weber has called for the swift establishment of migrant return hubs in Africa after tens of thousands of unauthorized migrants surged into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta in late July. In an op-ed for German outlet Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung that was published Monday, conservative boss Weber wrote: “Ceuta has shown that close cooperation with neighboring countries can work. Morocco immediately took people back. No one was able to travel onward into the Schengen area” and, he added, “Europe must quickly establish return hubs in Africa.” After tens of thousands forced their way into Ceuta — which is situated in North Africa — several international leaders pointed the finger at Spain’s left-wing government and its migration policy. Madrid had previously granted legal status to half a million unauthorized migrants . Advertisement Advertisement Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and her right-wing government are among the harshest critics, with Rome introducing border controls for travelers from Spain on Friday and sparking retaliation from Madrid. Weber echoed proposals made last week by EU Migration Commissioner Magnus Brunner, arguing that countries outside the bloc could be offered closer trade ties, economic collaboration and legal migration opportunities in exchange for accepting the installation of return hubs. “Migrants who have no right to remain must leave Europe — no ifs, ands or buts!” he wrote, adding that returns must no longer depend on the political will of individual member countries. Weber called for expanding the EU’s border and coast guard agency Frontex to 50,000 operational personnel, working alongside national forces and monitoring member countries’ compliance with the bloc’s border rules. Weber also rejected internal border controls within Europe as a long-term solution. “They may be necessary in exceptional situations. But they do not address the root cause of the problem … There can therefore be only one answer: strong, joint European protection of the external border.” In early June , the European Parliament and European Council announced new EU rules on migrant returns, including removals to countries outside the bloc in return hubs. Weber also argued that the Ceuta crisis, which left around 100 dead, was the result of unilateral national action and said that the Spanish government’s “political signals” have had “an immediate impact on migration routes.” This article has been updated. https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: SpaceX's mega rocket Starship makes a test flight from Starbase in Texas in May. Photograph: Eric Gay/AP View image in fullscreen SpaceX's mega rocket Starship makes a test flight from Starbase in Texas in May. Photograph: Eric Gay/AP Trump administration US judge declines to block transfer of wildlife refuge land to Musk’s SpaceX Environmental groups vow to continue opposition to deal that would expand site for Elon Musk rocket company Associated Press Mon 21 Sep 2026 19.54 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A federal judge on Monday refused to block the Trump administration from giving SpaceX more than 700 acres of wildlife refuge as part of a land swap in Texas, while environmental groups vowed to continue their legal challenge. US district judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr declined the plaintiffs’ request for a preliminary injunction to prevent the parcel exchange, saying they failed to prove it would worsen ecological risks to a Gulf coast region already transformed by billionaire Elon Musk’s rocket operations. In June, the US Fish and Wildlife Service approved moving forward with the deal with SpaceX , which would surrender 683 acres the company owns in exchange for the federal land in the Lower Rio Grande Valley National Wildlife Refuge. The 103,000-acre refuge spans four counties along the Texas border and is home to animal habitats and historical landmarks. Maps show the land SpaceX would acquire would be closer to the company’s launchpad near the US-Mexico border. The swap amounts to a gift of public lands to SpaceX, “clearing the way for bulldozers to tear into this wildlife refuge as soon as next week and turn a public treasure into a private payday”, said Laiken Jordahl, a spokesperson with the Center for Biological Diversity, which filed the lawsuit alongside other opponents including tribal groups. Jordahl said Monday that the litigation will continue even as the exchange goes forward. “This court order is not the final word. These lands hold incredible spiritual, historical and conservation value for the people and wildlife of South Texas . We won’t stop fighting to keep this irreplaceable public wildlife refuge safe from SpaceX bulldozers,” Jordahl said in a statement. The lawsuit asks the federal court to halt the exchange, which has worried SpaceX opponents in the area who have long criticized the company’s expanding footprint over lost access to beaches and concerns over exploding rockets. The Fish and Wildlife Service did not respond to a request for comment on Monday’s decision. Previously, a spokesperson had said the agency does not comment on ongoing litigation. The agency issued a final environmental assessment report in June that determined the exchange would cause no significant impact to the area. The report said the federal government believed the acquisition would represent a “net conservation benefit” and provide “substantial long-term conservation value and improving landscape-scale habitat connectivity across refuges in south Texas”. The judge said that the plaintiffs offered “relatively weak” evidence of environmental harm. “While they rightfully argue that the preservation of wildlife and historical lands furthers the public interest, they present no evidence demonstrating that the Property will suffer aesthetic, environmental, cultural, or historical degradation during the pendency of this lawsuit,” Rodriguez wrote in his ruling. In addition, the judge said a preliminary injunction would result in modifications to SpaceX’s development plans, “placing additional hardship on the company’s ability to meet milestones and contractual obligations”. SpaceX did not return an email seeking comment on the judge’s ruling. The space exploration company first broke ground in Texas more than a decade ago and has expanded rapidly, so much that SpaceX employees last year voted to incorporate their own local government called Starbase. https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/.text: Military Menu Introduction Systems Facilities Agencies Industry Operations Countries Hot Documents News Reports Policy Budget Congress Links WMD Intelligence Homeland Security Space Military Press statement by President Costa following the meeting with Prime Minister of Poland, Donald Tusk European Council / Council of the European Union European Council Statements and remarks 10 September 2026 14:30 Dear Prime Minister, dear Donald. First of all, thank you very much for your warm welcome here in Warsaw, and our very good talk as always. It is essential for me to listen directly to you, in your capital, to understand your national priorities and expectations - and to properly prepare the upcoming meetings of the European Council. That is why I am now visiting the capitals of member states. It has special meaning to be here with you dear Donald. Your experience and wisdom give you a unique voice in the European Council. All of our colleagues trust you, and with you, Polish positions, concerns and initiatives are highly valued. As a country on the European Union's eastern flank, Poland stands at the forefront of the security challenges facing our continent - and plays a vital role in shaping Europe's response to them. Our unwavering support for Ukraine matters: Ukraine is defending not only its own sovereignty, but Europe's security. And Poland, as Ukraine's neighbour and a key supporter of its defence, is playing a particularly important role in that effort. This is why strengthening our support for Ukraine must go hand in hand with strengthening our own collective preparedness and protecting our own borders. Russian threats highlight the need for Europe to ensure it has the capabilities to respond swiftly and effectively. We must continue our efforts to decisively strengthen Europe's defence readiness and ensure that we are prepared by 2030. Today, I discussed with Prime Minister Tusk, how the European Union budget for the period 2028-2034 will need to better address these new challenges we are facing. We need a European budget that gives us the means to deliver on our common priorities. Defence and security are key areas - as are competitiveness, innovation and strategic resilience. At the same time, the budget must continue to support our agricultural and cohesion policies, both essential to Europe's prosperity and development. Of course, like national budgets, the European Union budget must deliver on its priorities within the limits of finite resources. Most of it is financed through member states' national contributions. And we need to keep those contributions within reasonable limits. That is why a substantial package of so-called new own resources, the new revenue streams for the European Union, will be an essential part of an overall agreement. One thing is clear: we cannot afford any delay. We must reach an agreement by the end of this year to ensure that EU support for our farmers, businesses, students, researchers and innovators continues without interruption in 2028. The responsibility is ours. We must now engage in the final stage of these negotiations with determination and a European spirit. And I know I can count on you, Donald, and on your great experience with difficult European negotiations. Beyond our future budget, we need to make our economy stronger. A competitive Europe is a crucial element of our strategic autonomy. And I think that Europe has a lot to learn from Poland's economic success story. Europe needs to create better conditions for European industries and businesses to innovate, thrive and grow. And better opportunities and quality jobs for our citizens. This is what the European Union's "One Europe, One Market" agenda is all about. We need to accelerate its implementation. That agenda also focuses on affordable energy. This is fundamental for Europe's competitiveness, especially for our industry. Ensuring affordable and competitive energy prices is key, both for our citizens and for our industry. Therefore, we need to intensify our work to reduce energy costs, while pursuing our efforts on the clean transition and decarbonisation in a technology-neutral way - that means, nuclear or renewables. Also here, Poland's performance has been very impressive, especially considering its historical legacy. Europe's strength lies in our unity. And Poland's voice is an essential part of that strength. By bringing our efforts together, we can build a Union that is more secure, more competitive, and better prepared to meet the challenges of the future. Thank you very much.

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqgm.text: Figure caption, By Henry Moore Published 30 September 2026 Updated 52 minutes ago A pilot has been arrested after he stabbed the other pilot on a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv and "apparently tried to crash the plane", Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said. Passengers and crew overpowered the attacker and retook control of the Flydubai aircraft, landing it safely at an airport in Tabuk, northwestern Saudi Arabia, with more than 170 people on board. The passengers, who were almost all Israeli, arrived later on Wednesday in Tel Aviv on a repatriation flight. The stabbed pilot, named as Indian national Captain Smit Machchhar, has been taken to hospital but is reported to be in a stable condition. Netanyahu and India's leader Narendra Modi praised him as a "hero". "Despite being stabbed and seriously injured, he fought back, resisted, opened the cockpit door, and enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker â preventing a catastrophic mid-air disaster," Netanyahu wrote on X. "He saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals." The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia said Machchhar was in a stable condition in hospital. Modi praised the pilot's actions, writing on X: "In the face of the gravest danger and despite being seriously injured, he showed immense courage and an unwavering resolve to protect the lives of others. "India is proud of Captain Machchhar." Image source, EPA Image caption, Passengers arrived in Tel Aviv after their original flight was forced to land in Saudi Arabia No motive for the incident has been given and the pilot was under investigation in Saudi Arabia, Netanyahu told Fox News on Wednesday night, before he was expected to be taken back to the United Arab Emirates (UAE), where the flight took off from. Israel was "likely" to contribute to the investigation, the prime minister added. US President Donald Trump said he had spoken with Netanyahu following the incident, saying it seemed as though the attacker was "perhaps a terrorist" or there were other reasons behind the attack. Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz has also called it an "attempted jihadist terror attack", without giving any details. Flydubai's flight FZ1073 took off from Dubai International Airport in the UAE at 03:05 GMT (07:05 local time), en route to Ben-Gurion Airport in Israel. Around two and a half hours into its journey, data from flight tracking website Flightrader24 reported a rapid descent over Saudi Arabia, dropping more than 17,000 feet (over 5,000m) in less than two minutes. Minutes later, the plane signalled an emergency code - squawk 7700 - before switching it to a squawk 7500 code reporting a hijacking. Around 20 minutes after these codes were signalled, the plane looped back into Saudi Arabia, where it later started its manual descent for landing. Less than an hour later, the plane returned to squawk 7700. Shortly after the incident, the Israeli and Saudi Arabian air forces dispatched fighter jets, while Netanyahu held urgent consultations. Initial media reports suggested a fight had broken out between the aircraft's two pilots, causing the rapid descent and landing. However, in the hours after the plane touched down in Tabuk, eyewitness accounts and a statement by Netanyahu confirmed one of the pilots had stabbed the other and, according to the Israeli prime minister, "apparently tried to crash" the aircraft. He said an Israeli passenger told him "the plane went into a spin and began to descend" before the passenger and a crew member entered the cockpit and overpowered the "pilot who had carried out the stabbing". Two on-duty crew travelling on the flight were then able to land the plane safely, Flydubai said. In an address on Wednesday evening, Netanyahu called the situation "a very serious security incident" and said Israeli security forces were "maintaining close contact with the relevant authorities to ensure the continued safety of the passengers". Unlike Israel's defence minister, Netanyahu did not give a motive for the incident. "I salute these heroes who demonstrated extraordinary resourcefulness and courage," he added. "They saved many lives and prevented a major disaster." Image source, Reuters Flydubai said in a statement that "an altercation occurred in the flight deck" and the flight was "successfully secured by on-duty Flydubai crew travelling on the flight, who diverted and landed the aircraft safely at Tabuk airport". An airline spokesperson added: "Our immediate priority is to ensure the ongoing safety, health, and wellbeing of all passengers and crew members involved in this incident and support the official investigation." The passengers who had been on board flight FZ1073 arrived in Tel Aviv at around 18:40 local time (15:40 GMT). They were greeted at the airport by crowds of onlookers playing music, singing, dancing and waving Israeli flags. A number of people were "very emotional and crying as they came off the plane," a paramedic from Israel's ambulance service told the BBC. One passenger, Yaniv Hayun, met Netanyahu and told him how he and others on the flight had restrained the attacker. "The pilot who was stabbed was simply very close to the door, so it was hard for us to open it," Hayun said in a video posted on social media by the prime minister's office, but before the stabbed pilot - now identified as Machchhar - collapsed, he was able to open the door. Yaniv said he put the attacker, who was trying to disable the plane, in a chokehold before other passengers helped pin him down. He added that he "pulled the controls" of the plane and after it levelled out, another pilot took over control. Figure caption, Zvika Meness, another passenger, told Israeli public broadcaster Kan News that he and other passengers tied the attacker up "with his own zip ties and with the multimedia headphones". He said: "There are children and families here who have been through a very severe, highly traumatic event." https://enrsi.stvr.sk/articles/news/4611.text: House Chair Richard Raši (Hlas-SD) met the President of the National Council of Austria Walter Rosenkranz and Speaker of the Czech Chamber of Deputies Tomio Okamura in the Austrian region of Wachau during a meeting held under the Austerlitz Format (S3: Austria, the Czech Republic and Slovakia). The event follows up on a meeting in Bratislava in December and will also be the first meeting at the highest political level during Austria's presidency of the S3. "When we met in Bratislava on 3 December of last year during Slovakia's presidency of the Austerlitz Format, we agreed that cooperation between our parliaments must deliver concrete results. This dialogue will continue at the meeting in Austria. The Austerlitz Format has a firm place in Central Europe, bringing together three neighbouring countries that share common interests, exchange experience and coordinate their stances on European issues," said Raši. The main purpose of the trip is to strengthen practical inter-parliamentary cooperation between Slovakia, the Czech Republic and Austria. The speakers of the three parliaments will discuss current challenges related to the enlargement of the European Union (EU), migration and the involvement of young people in public life. The second thematic block will focus on the digital transformation of parliaments and the responsible use of artificial intelligence. In addition to discussing the protection of borders, Raši said that he'll also present Slovakia's experience with youth parliaments and student internships. According to him, support for well-prepared candidate countries in the Western Balkans will be important as well. The talks will also revolve around exchanges of experience in modernising parliamentary work and the responsible use of artificial intelligence, focusing on how digital tools can streamline the work of parliaments and improve public access to their activities. With his partners, Raši also wants to discuss data security, the protection of sensitive information, the development of digital skills and opportunities for cooperation among parliamentary administrations. The event hosted by the Austrians kicked off on Thursday with a working dinner of the parliamentary speakers in Durnstein. On Friday (18 September), a brief working meeting will be held, followed by the main session at Gottweig Abbey. Austria took over the presidency of the Austerlitz Format from Slovakia on 1 July 2026, and, based on a rotating principle, the Czech Republic will become the presiding country as of July 2027. Source: TASR

https://nltimes.nl/2026/10/17/online-sho.text: Image Dachau Concentration Camp gate - Credit: Rapsar / Wikimedia Commons - License: CC-BY-SA Politics Wilbrink Dutch Dachau Committee Bruna Amazon Bol.com Dachau concentration camp Dachau » More tags « Less tags Share this article: Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Online shops pull 99-year-old's book after claims of Dachau captivity found improbable Saturday, 17 October 2026 - 14:45 Online retailers have ceased selling the biography of 99-year-old Willem Wilbrink following a controversy that arose last week over his accounts of the Second World War. According to an investigation by Historisch Nieuwsblad, his narrative of being imprisoned in the Dachau concentration camp was highly improbable. Investigators found no camp number for Wilbrink in Dachau’s records, and other survivors did not recognize his accounts, among other factors. Bol.com has removed the book titled Getekend voor het leven in Dachau en Indië by Laurens van Aggelen at the publisher’s request, according to NOS. Bruna and Amazon have also stopped stocking the book, according to the book trade journal Boekblad. According to Wilbrink, he was arrested at the age of 15 for participating in the resistance. He said he had to carry bodies in the Dachau concentration camp. He wrote that he discovered certain individuals marked for the crematorium were still alive and took them to the sick bay. Researchers who examined Wilbrink’s wartime record report finding no corroboration for his claims. He allegedly has no camp number attached to his name. Dachau’s record keeping is reportedly known for exceptional accuracy, researchers said. On top of that, other survivors did not recognize Wilbrink’s stories. He also wears decorations whose provenance is unclear, including a Polish “hero title.” The Dutch Dachau Committee has reportedly known since 2024 that doubts existed about Wilbrink’s story. The committee did not actively publicize doubts because “we, more than anyone, know what wartime trauma can do to the stories in one’s head,” chairman Jaeger said on Friday. According to Jaeger, Wilbrink himself believes he was imprisoned at the camp. Following the news, the NIOD Institute for War, Holocaust, and Genocide Studies warned narratives of this kind can damage the historical record of the Second World War. The institute noted that those who deliberately seek to sow doubt can exploit such stories to cast doubt on the Holocaust. Kateryna Klochko - AP Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged supporters Saturday to speak out in favor of new U.S. sanctions against Russia, hours after President Donald Trump signed an executive order putting the sweeping restrictions on hold. The White House decision has heightened fears that Ukraine could be left exposed to Moscow’s escalating attacks as winter approaches. In a social media statement, Zelenskyy called Trump’s decision unfortunate but avoided directly criticizing the U.S. leader despite deepening tensions between Ukraine and Washington in recent days. “A decision was unfortunately made in America to completely disregard the Lindsey Graham Act, which was supposed to impose truly effective pressure on Russia to bring this war to an end,” Zelenskyy wrote. “This Act could have helped enormously – and still can! But it needs to actually work, and every voice in support of it matters.” He separately thanked Democrats and Republicans who supported the legislation, saying that blocking it would encourage Russia to continue killing and that limiting Ukraine’s ability to retaliate would not bring peace. “Nevertheless, we very much hope — and I personally hope — that the president of the United States of America will do everything possible to make (Russian President Vladimir) Putin stop the killing, stop the attacks on our energy infrastructure, and end this war,” he said. Trump told reporters Saturday that they don’t know what his decision is yet regarding sanctions in Russia, despite the executive order he signed Friday night waiving sanctions, citing a U.S national interest. “We’ll figure it out, and you’ll figure it out. But it’s a very good decision, and it’s going to be a decision that’s good for the country, and I think good for the world,” Trump said at a fundraising dinner at his Florida estate. He then didn’t answer any follow up questions and the rest of the dinner was closed to the press. Asked about contacts with Washington, Zelenskyy said Ukraine’s lead negotiator, Rustem Umerov, had met Friday with U.S. presidential envoy Jared Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law. Zelenskyy said the U.S. was working to arrange a three-way meeting involving him, Trump and Putin, potentially in the Middle East, Europe or the United States. Overnight Russian attacks killed at least four people, including an ambulance driver, and wounded dozens, officials said. Critics say Trump's decision helps Putin Named after late South Carolina Sen. Lindsey Graham , the legislation had sought to clamp down more quickly on the flow of financial resources fueling Russia's 4 1/2-year-old war against Ukraine . The bill had sought to sanction Russian officials, banks and a shadow fleet of tankers that keeps Russian energy moving. Trump personally signed the legislation just last month and his move came just two days before a deadline set in the law itself for its implementation. Trump told Congress that the pause was in the national interest but gave no further details. Sen. Richard Blumenthal, who co-drafted the bill, criticized Trump's move, saying the president was turning his back on “the majority of Americans, their representatives in both houses of Congress, and our European allies.” “These waivers have nothing to do with our national security, and everything to do with sucking up to Vladimir Putin,” Blumenthal said. Trump’s unexpected decision comes a week after he had agreed to purchase diesel from Russia to try to bring down global energy prices, despite that potentially hurting Ukraine. Republicans and Democrats alike say the purchase will help Russia execute its war against Ukraine — without making a difference to global fuel prices, which are elevated mostly due to Trump’s war on Iran. Starlink restrictions were planned, Zelenskyy says Zelenskyy said that Kyiv was investigating sudden speed restrictions on Ukraine’s use of Starshield , the military-grade version of SpaceX’s Starlink satellite internet service, which is the backbone of Ukraine’s drone operations and communication. The restrictions, imposed without warning early Thursday, cut the internet data connection when a communication terminal moves faster than 160 kph (100 mph). The cap forced Ukrainian drones to fly slower than usual, making it easier for Russian weapons to target or evade them. Zelenskyy said that there were no similar restrictions in European Union countries and that they apply only to Ukraine. “In other words, this is a planned operation,” he said. It was unclear who was responsible. SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk said this week that the U.S. government owns and controls the system, with decisions about its use resting with the U.S. military and, ultimately, the president. The Pentagon has not answered questions from The Associated Press about the restrictions. Trump told reporters Friday that he did not order restrictions on the system. He also doubted that the disruption came from Musk. “Well, I don’t know if it was anybody, but it wasn’t me, and I don’t think it was Elon,” Trump said. “And from what I understand, it’s the same as it’s always been.” On Saturday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the White House was not behind the reduction in service to SpaceX’s Starlink. “It wasn’t deliberate,” he told reporters before departing for Uzbekistan. “We had nothing to do with it.” “The United States, nobody ordered that Starlink speed to be slowed down,” Rubio, who also serves as Trump’s national security adviser, added. “It sort of happened.” Rubio, though, said Ukraine does not have access to the Pentagon-owned military-grade Starshield system. “I know Ukraine wants access to Starshield. They do not have Star Shield now. They’ve asked for access to it in order to conduct deep strikes inside of Russia. They do not have access to it at this moment. Those are two different products," he said. Kyiv reports a ‘massive’ energy strike Moscow carried out a massive strike on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure, targeting more than 15 sites across the country, Zelenskyy said. “The sheer scale and unrelenting pace of Russia’s strikes, specifically against our energy sector, are unfortunately having severe consequences,” he said. Ukraine’s air force said it intercepted all four of Russia's cruise missiles and most of the 332 attack drones it fired overnight. Russia’s heavy bombardment of the power grid ahead of winter has been an annual feature of the war, aimed at wearing down Ukraine’s appetite for the fight by denying civilians heat and running water. Ukrainian officials have warned that Russia is stockpiling ballistic missiles for more attacks in the coming months. Russian attacks killed three people in the Ukrainian city of Sloviansk, Vadym Liakh, head of the city military administration, said Saturday. A Russian strike also killed an ambulance driver in Ukraine’s Kherson region, head of the local military administration Yaroslav Shanko said. The strike, which used guided bombs, wounded at least 33 others, he said. Romania downs 2 drones over Black Sea Romania’s Ministry of National Defense said Saturday that its pilots had shot down two drones over the country’s territorial waters in the Black Sea. Two F-16s were scrambled at 5:43 p.m. local time after radar systems “detected a group of aerial targets moving southwest, approximately 120 kilometers east of Snake Island,” the ministry said. The drones entered the NATO member’s airspace around 6 p.m. and were shot down minutes later. “Both aerial targets were identified as drones and were shot down over Romania’s territorial waters,” the ministry said. It later identified the drones as jet-powered and from “Geran family,” which are types of drones Moscow has used in Ukraine. The incident follows a spate of drone attacks on at least seven cargo vessels off the Black Sea coasts of NATO members Romania and Bulgaria in October. Scores of drones have crossed into Romanian airspace over the past two years, with officials attributing many of the incursions to Russia. Romania first shot down drones this year , marking its first such action since Moscow invaded neighboring Ukraine. Davies reported from Manchester, England.
